title: The Burning Choir Anew
premise: August Kavanagh, an exiled storm-caller hiding in the magic-dead valley of Hollowmere, is dragged back into the world when the old gods resume answering prayers — and one of them answers through him. He joins a ragged found family of pilgrims and deserters to reach the capital, where King Aldric has been hollowed out by a god wearing his crown like a parasite. To save the king, August must unbind the god using the inheritance of storm-song his mother died protecting, but doing so means choosing between the duty that exiled him and the love he found on the road. In the end August shatters the crown-god at the cost of his own magic, frees Aldric, and chooses to stay with his found family rather than reclaim his lost home.
about_author: Bram Winterbourne is the pen name of a former choir singer who claims to have once heard a hymn answered from inside a thunderhead. They write fantasy about stubborn people, terrible weather, and gods who should have stayed asleep.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: POV August. Years after exile, August lives quietly in Hollowmere, mending roofs and refusing to remember his storm-calling. When a dying pilgrim crawls into the valley carrying a prayer-stone that hums with impossible life, the stone answers August's involuntary whisper. Emotional beat: dread awakening — the past has found him.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: POV August. The prayer-stone burns itself out delivering a message meant for another man: the king is dying, and something else is answering in his voice. Valley elders demand August destroy the stone; instead he hides it. Emotional beat: guilt and defiance as August realizes exile was never safety, only delay.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: POV August. Hunters arrive seeking the stone, forcing August to flee the only home he has left, guided by the pilgrim's sister, Sera Vane, a disgraced battle-priestess. Crossing the valley's edge, his dormant magic stirs for the first time in years. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration — leaving the cage.

chapters.title: Sera Vane's Broken Order
chapters.summary: POV Sera. On the road, Sera reveals her order branded her a heretic for claiming the gods had gone silent long before they supposedly did. She tests August's storm-song with a hymn; it answers too eagerly. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two people discarded by their institutions.

chapters.title: The Choir of Little Saints
chapters.summary: POV August. They fall in with a traveling troupe of orphaned god-touched children led by Tam, a pickpocket who can hear prayers. One child's innocent prayer is answered instantly — proof the old gods are awake and listening everywhere. Emotional beat: warmth of found family shadowed by rising wrongness.

chapters.title: What the Wells Remember
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In a river town, every well water tastes of ash and every prayer gets the same reply: 'Soon.' An old priest recognizes August's surname and calls him heir of the Stormbound line. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as burden rather than gift.

chapters.title: The First Thunder
chapters.summary: POV August. Crown-hunters ambush the group; cornered, August unleashes a storm for the first time since exile and nearly kills Tam doing it. Horrified by his own power, he swears to bind it again. Emotional beat: self-loathing colliding with the children's awe.

chapters.title: Letters From a Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV Sera. A royal courier, deserter Wren Ashfall, defects to them carrying the king's private letters — lucid pleas hidden inside official decrees written in someone else's hand. Emotional beat: hope that the king still fights, and horror at what writes for him.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV August. At a ruined shrine, Sera's order archives reveal the truth: the crown-god is Vessel, an old god of obedience once bound beneath the capital, now wearing Aldric. August learns his bloodline made the original binding. Emotional beat: destiny tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Tam's Terrible Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Tam secretly prays for the strength to protect the children — and something answers, offering power at a price. August catches him mid-ritual and breaks it, nearly losing Tam's trust forever. Emotional beat: fear that love makes everyone vulnerable to the listening dark.

chapters.title: The City of Bells
chapters.summary: POV August. The group reaches the capital, where every bell rings unstruck at dawn and citizens smile too easily, their doubts smoothed away. They infiltrate via Wren's old garrison contacts. Emotional beat: claustrophobic wrongness — a city under a lullaby.

chapters.title: Audience With the Smiling Court
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Disguised as pilgrims, they witness the king hold court: Aldric's body moves, grants mercy generously, and speaks in perfect unison with the bells. Only his eyes beg. Emotional beat: revulsion and pity entwined.

chapters.title: The King in the Mirror Room
chapters.summary: POV August. Using the prayer-stone's last fragment, August reaches Aldric's sealed mind and meets the real king — a man who remembers his name but not his son's face. Aldric begs him to end it, even if it means ending him. Emotional beat: compassion against the coming cost.

chapters.title: Stormsong, Recovered
chapters.summary: POV Sera. In the palace vaults, Sera finds the Stormbound inheritance: a bone-white tuning fork and August's mother's final hymn, which she died smuggling out. August refuses to read it, fearing what the song will demand. Emotional beat: grief finally given a voice.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: POV Tam. A child of the choir, desperate and homesick, betrays their location to the crown-guard. Tam takes a blade meant for August; the group scatters into the city's underways. Emotional beat: heartbreak — found family wounded by its youngest member's longing.

chapters.title: The Underways
chapters.summary: POV August. Hiding in flooded catacombs, August finally sings his mother's hymn alone and understands: the binding requires a willing vessel to take Vessel's place. The song was always a trap with a kind face. Emotional beat: cold clarity — there is no clean way out.

chapters.title: What Duty Demands
chapters.summary: POV Sera. Sera argues August must take the binding himself; August refuses to abandon the family they've become. Their fight cracks open old wounds — her heresy, his exile — and ends in exhausted honesty rather than victory. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: POV August. Vessel announces a grand consecration to bind the whole city's faith permanently. The group resolves to strike during the rite, with Wren turning his garrison and the forgiven child carrying the tuning fork. Emotional beat: grim resolve forged from failure.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV August. Amid the consecration, August sings the full storm-song, tearing Vessel loose from Aldric as lightning splits the cathedral bells. But the unbinding demands a vessel, and the god turns its hunger toward the children. Emotional beat: climax — everything given at once.

chapters.title: The Empty Crown
chapters.summary: POV Sera. August offers himself instead, pouring his storm-magic into the binding until Vessel starves and crumbles, leaving August ordinary — mortal, magicless, alive. Aldric wakes in his own body, weeping. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs exactly what it promised.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: POV August. Recovery: Aldric pardons the Stormbound line and offers August land, title, restoration. August declines the valley's pardon too — Hollowmere was never home anymore. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with what was lost and what was chosen.

chapters.title: The Burning Choir, Singing
chapters.summary: POV August. One year later, August teaches the god-touched children to sing safely, Sera rebuilds a kinder order, and Tam keeps watch over the sealed shrine. When rain comes, it is only rain. Emotional beat: peace earned — family chosen over inheritance, love over duty.
